name: Crushed limestone sand and grit, 0/6 mm (the Paris gardens' 'sable'; limestone screenings)
summary: Limestone crushed and screened to a sand-and-grit of 0 to 6 mm with its own fines: the pale, dusty surface of the French formal garden's walks (the stabilise of the Tuileries), and the sharp limestone screenings that bed and joint stone paving. In the museum it is the grounds' walks and the cour round the canal, the walk east and the Elan's terrace (rolled), and the sand in the joints of the grounds' stone paving. It ties to the stone family as the same calcite, broken small.

constituents.material: fines (the dust fraction produced by crushing)
constituents.role: fill the voids and bind the surface when wetted and rolled

formation.how: Quarried limestone is crushed and screened; the 0/6 fraction keeps everything that passes a 6.3 mm sieve, from grit down to dust. The grains are angular, which is why the material locks together when wetted and rolled; river sand, rounded, does not.

optics.kind: granular dielectric: angular calcite grains and dust; diffuse, with glints from cleavage faces

grainF0.derivation: as the travertine record: F = ((n - 1)/(n + 1))^2 averaged over randomly oriented calcite grains (n_o 1.6583, n_e 1.4861 at 589.3 nm)
grainF0.source: Ghosh G. (1999) 'Dispersion-equation coefficients for the refractive index and birefringence of calcite and quartz crystals', Optics Communications 163:95-102; coefficients as tabulated at https://refractiveindex.info/?shelf=main&book=CaCO3&page=Ghosh-o and https://refractiveindex.info/?shelf=main&book=CaCO3&page=Ghosh-e
grainF0.conditions: a single grain face; a granular bed's reflectance is dominated by multiple scattering, not by this

wet.text: Wet, the gravel darkens: water in the pores and on the grains lowers the index step and traps diffusely reflected light by total internal reflection in the film.
wet.source: J. Lekner, M.C. Dorf (1988) 'Why some things are darker when wet', Applied Optics 27(7):1278-1280, https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.27.001278

wet.text: Wet and dry surfaces differ in reflectance through the same mechanism in soils and sands; the darkening is largest for bright, strongly scattering materials.
wet.source: S.A. Twomey, C.F. Bohren, J.L. Mergenthaler (1986) 'Reflectance and albedo differences between wet and dry surfaces', Applied Optics 25(3):431-437, https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.25.000431
wet.note: Qualitative summary; the paper's numbers were not read.

photograph: Pale beige-grey grit with small angular stones; paler and smoother in the trodden lanes, darker and looser at the edges.
Dust on shoes and on the lower edge of hedges and benches in a dry summer; a darker, uniformly damp surface after rain, drying from the crown of the walk.
Shallow puddles in low spots after rain, with a rim of washed-out fines when they dry.
The grains' faces glint in low sun.
Up close: angular grains up to about 6 mm set in compacted fines, with loose grit on top swept into low ridges at the edges of the lanes.

evidenceRejected.shows: Rounded river pebbles of mixed rock, grey, rust-red and green, with no fines between them: not a crushed limestone and not a rolled walk.

evidenceSearch.tier: Tier (a) is thin: grading, grain mineral and trade practice. A tier (b) specimen closes the gap: a calibrated photograph of a Paris stabilise walk (Tuileries or Luxembourg), dry and wet, trodden lane and edge, with a ColorChecker.

unverified.reason: No colorimetric or reflectance measurement of a limestone walk was read. A search summary cites solar reflectances of about 0.42-0.45 for unbound limestone aggregates (ASTM E1918), not read at the source.
The old build's gravel BaseColor #BDAF94 and trodden-lane colour #D6CBB2 (windows/Scripts/exterior_materials.py), chosen by eye. Not measurements.
A search summary describes the Tuileries' stabilise as 'un melange de chaux, de gravier et de sable'; the article was not readable (lejdd.fr, 403).
No friction or slip measurement for rolled limestone walks was read.

Via Materiaux lists 'Masse volumique: 1.7' for its crushed limestone 0/6 without a unit; t/m3 is assumed. Source: Via Materiaux (Annecy), 'Sable 0/6 concasse calcaire - Vrac', product page read 2026-09-26, https://viamateriaux.fr/produit/sable-0-6-concasse-calcaire/
No measured octave-band absorption of a compacted limestone walk was read; the table is derived from a ground class.
